summary: Ua Chang Seng is a traditional takeaway bakery in Chiang Mai’s Chang Moi/Kad Luang district, known for khanom khai (small baked egg cakes) and a range of Chinese-style sweets. TAT includes it in an evening dessert route toward Warorot Market; a Wongnai review from January 2026 suggests it was still trading this year.
whyGo: Try the old-style khanom khai at a shop specifically recommended by Thailand’s tourism authority.
Browse other traditional sweets and combine a short stop with Warorot Market and nearby Ton Lam Yai.
bestFor: Travelers seeking an inexpensive local sweet or takeaway bakery stop.
A brief snack break while exploring Chang Moi and the Kad Luang market area.
skipIf: You avoid eggs or need confirmed allergen controls; ingredient and cross-contact details are not published.
You need a sit-down café or guaranteed step-free access; neither is documented.
duration: Allow about 10–20 minutes to choose and buy sweets; treat this as a planning estimate.
cost: Wongnai lists khanom khai at ฿45 per bag and other small sweets at ฿15 each; a January 2026 reviewer described spending under ฿100 per person. Prices and portions may change before December 2026; bring small cash.
hours: Wongnai showed the shop as open until 19:30 when checked, but a complete weekly schedule was not available. Confirm directly near your visit, especially around year-end holidays.
bestTime: Visit in the daytime or early evening while the listing indicates it is open, and ask whether fresh cakes are available. TAT places it on an evening dessert route, but baking times are unconfirmed.
gettingThere: The listed address is 36/3 Chang Moi Tat Mai Road, Chang Moi, opposite Wat Nam Tharee/Wat Khaek in the Warorot Market area. Walk from nearby Kad Luang/Warorot; from elsewhere in central Chiang Mai, use a songthaew, tuk-tuk or ride-hail and walk the last stretch. Wongnai reviews describe limited curbside parking, so a drop-off is more practical.
booking: No booking is indicated; this is a takeaway shop. Walk in and buy while items are available. The listing gives 053-232-268 and 053-413-125 for checking hours or stock; English support is unconfirmed.
accessibility: Formal accessibility information was not found. Sources describe a street-front shop focused on takeaway; entrance step, counter access, seating and accessible toilet are unconfirmed. The surrounding market streets may be busy.
practicalTips: Khanom khai is an egg cake; ask about ingredients if you have allergies. Wheat, dairy and cross-contact information is not published.
Show the Thai name อื้อชั่งเซ้ง or ask for ขนมไข่ (khanom khai) if language is a barrier.
Ask the price and whether sweets are sold by bag or piece before ordering; the shop offers several kinds.
Pair the stop with Warorot Market and the nearby Ton Lam Yai area.
decemberNotes: This can work as a short Chiang Mai market-district stop during a December day or early evening. No December 2026 event or holiday-hours notice was found. Recheck the listing or call before making a dedicated trip, as year-end hours and stock may vary.
uncertainties: TAT’s recommendation dates to 2020. Wongnai has a January 2026 review and a current address listing, but December 2026 operation is not guaranteed.
The listed closing time is not a verified weekly schedule; baking times and daily stock are unknown.
Menu prices are indicative listing/member-submitted prices, not an official published price list.
Accessibility, detailed ingredients and holiday opening hours are not documented.
